sections.html:
Southfield residential sales now run through a point-of-sale inspection, and that step sets the pace of a closing. City Council approved the program in April 2026 as Ordinance 1835, so schedule the inspection before you commit to a closing date.

A seller can go three ways:

  • Agent listing: showings, the buyer's loan and the city inspection all stack up on the calendar.
  • Private sale: you find the buyer and manage the contract with a title company.
  • Cash sale as-is: the buyer takes the house with whatever the inspection cites. Settle who pays for those repairs before you sign.

Because the program is new, ask the Building Department how it treats a sale that is already under contract, and keep the inspection report with your closing file.

sections.h2: How the inspection works and what it costs
sections.html:
The Building and Safety Engineering department inspects the house and issues a Certificate of Occupancy after violations are cleared. Its Point of Sale packet walks through the steps, and you apply on the city's online BS&A portal.

Southfield resale inspection fee, $190 total
Fee componentAmount
Application$40
Certificate$50
Building trade, reinspection included$100
  • Payment comes first. Staff then book the visit within 14 days of the payment date.
  • A person has to stay at the house for the whole window, either 9:30 to 12:30 or 12:30 to 3:30.
  • Sellers can repair the listed items and ask for a follow-up visit, which the fee covers.
  • Alternatively, buyer and seller both sign an Affidavit to Assume Resale Violations before closing, and the buyer gets 30 days afterward to finish the work.

The affidavit calls for a performance bond sized to the repairs and bars occupancy until the work passes reinspection. Life safety items must be corrected before anyone moves in. The Building Department answers questions at 248-796-4100.

Southfield is about 15 miles northwest of downtown Detroit, with a July 2025 estimate of 76,111 residents. Owners live in only 53.4 percent of housing units, which makes rentals common. The typical owner-occupied home is worth $236,200 and typical gross rent is $1,340. Owner monthly cost is $1,779 with a mortgage and $764 without. The city has 34,860 households with a median income of $68,166.

Lathrup Village, a separate city, sits as an enclave inside the eastern part of Southfield. The main streets form a one-mile grid, with 9 through 12 Mile Roads running east to west and Telegraph, Lahser, Evergreen and Greenfield north to south. M-10 (the Lodge), I-696, M-39 and US-24 cross the city, and SMART buses cover local and regional lines.

Southfield Public Schools runs the city's schools. Part of the north sends students to Birmingham and the southeast corner to Oak Park, so confirm a street with the district.

sections.h2: Preparing a Southfield house for the inspection
sections.html:
Phone the Building Department and ask what the inspector reviews at your address. Check the file for permits that were pulled and never closed out. The packet includes a Furnace / Boiler Certification form with carbon monoxide readings, so a city-registered contractor should service the heating system first.

The 14-day scheduling window only starts after payment, so pay early. Collect your deed, payoff figure and permit records for the title company, and draft the repair affidavit ahead of time if the buyer will take on the work.

sections.h2: Recording at the Oakland County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Oakland County's Register of Deeds in Pontiac (248-858-0597) takes the deed after the county Treasurer's Office has certified taxes on any warranty deed, warranty-clause deed or land contract. The office asks for original signatures, a notary acknowledgment on Michigan documents, the buyer's address on the deed and a 2.5 inch top margin on page one.

Call the office for the current recording fee and the county transfer tax rate before you pick a closing date.

The Building Department's forms include a Rental Registration form, a Vacant Building Registration Application and vacant building owner and purchaser affidavits. Ask which ones apply to your address before you list.

A rented house adds scheduling work, since someone has to be present for the inspection. A vacant house should be secured, heated in cold months and cleared of debris, so the inspector sees its true condition.

Pay the inspection fee as soon as you sign a contract, because the 14-day window runs from the payment date. After the visit, decide whether to fix the cited items yourself or let the buyer assume them through the affidavit. Meanwhile the title company orders the tax certification and prepares the deed. Close only after the Certificate of Occupancy is issued or the affidavit and bond are in place. Keep every receipt and the inspection report in one folder so the title company and the buyer see the same record, and ask the Building Department before closing whether anything is still open on the address.

Ask the Building Department for the Point of Sale packet and read the checklist before you pay. Inspectors cite life safety items first, and those must be corrected before anyone moves in. Heating equipment gets special attention, which is why the packet carries the Furnace / Boiler Certification form with carbon monoxide readings.

Walk the house yourself with the checklist. Look at smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, stair rails, electrical covers, plumbing leaks and exterior upkeep. Small fixes you make before the visit cost less than a reinspection request, even though the fee already covers one follow-up.

The contract decides who pays. In an agent sale, the buyer's lender may insist that the seller fix the cited items. In a cash sale, the buyer may accept the house as it stands and sign the Affidavit to Assume Resale Violations, then finish the work within 30 days with a performance bond in place. Whatever you agree, get it in writing and keep the signed affidavit and the inspection report in your closing file.

If the house is rented, schedule a time when the tenant or a representative can stay for the full window. If it is vacant, arrange for someone to open the house and stay.

Gather the deed, your mortgage payoff figure, permit records and any contractor receipts for recent work. Ask the title company which tax certification it needs from the Oakland County Treasurer's Office, since warranty deeds and land contracts need one before recording. Keep the Certificate of Occupancy with the deed copy once the city issues it, and hand a copy to the buyer. Write down the date each fee was paid so you can answer any question the title company raises later.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection before selling in Southfield?
faqs.a: Yes. Ordinance 1835, approved in April 2026, calls for point-of-sale inspections on residential homes. The fee is $190, and a Certificate of Occupancy follows once violations are fixed.

faqs.q: Can the buyer take over the inspector's repair list?
faqs.a: Yes. Both parties sign an Affidavit to Assume Resale Violations before closing. The buyer then has 30 days to finish repairs, and a performance bond is required.

faqs.q: How soon does Southfield schedule the inspection?
faqs.a: Within 14 days of payment. A person must stay at the house through the full morning or afternoon window.

faqs.q: Where do I record a Southfield deed?
faqs.a: Oakland County's Register of Deeds, at 248-858-0597. A warranty deed or land contract needs certification from the county Treasurer's Office before it is recorded.

faqs.q: Does paying cash avoid the Southfield inspection?
faqs.a: No. Point-of-sale rules cover residential sales however they are financed. A cash buyer may take on the cited repairs through the affidavit and keep the closing moving.
